In https://github.com/suhr/iris-tutorial I started to port iris-tutorial to Lean. Here's some problems met so far:

  • You can't write ⊢ P -∗ (P -∗ Q) -∗ Q as simply P -∗ (P -∗ Q) -∗ Q in iris-lean
  • The tutorial needs iapply but there's no such tactic in iris-lean yet

suhr said:

  • You can't write ⊢ P -∗ (P -∗ Q) -∗ Q as simply P -∗ (P -∗ Q) -∗ Q in iris-lean

I think this is not likely to get better. You could get iprop(P -∗ (P -∗ Q) -∗ Q) to work but that's not really better.

I tired of waiting for https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/pull/80 to be merged, so I filled the rest of Basics.lean using a fork of the repo.

There are three unproven lemmas remaining, which use ⊣⊢. In the tutorial, bi-entails is split with iSplit, but in iris-lean isplit does not work for ⊣⊢.
But constructor works fine for ⊣⊢

Now I'm trying to port pure.v, but theorem eq_elm {A} (P : A → iProp σ) (x y : A) : (⌜x = y⌝ : IProp σ) -∗ P x -∗ P y := sorry gives me the following error: error: IrisTutorial/Pure.lean:39:49: elaboration function for 'Iris.BI.BIBase.«term_-∗_»' has not been implemented.
I think you should put your main goal a ⊢. Enclosing it in iprop(...) might also work.
Huh, I forgot about the ⊢ thing again. Thanks!
Now both basics.v and pure.v are ported, and the rest of tutorial requires heaplang.

Now we have some bits of HeapLang, so I tried to update iris-lean in iris-tutorial. Unfortunately, some proof that used to work does not work anymore.

Specifically, this used to work:

theorem sep_ex_distr {A} (P : IProp σ) (Φ : A → IProp σ) :
    (P ∗ ∃ x, Φ x) ⊣⊢ ∃ x, P ∗ Φ x := by
  constructor
  · iintro ⟨hp, x, fx⟩
    iexists x
    isplitl [hp]
    · iexact hp
    · iexact fx
  · iintro ⟨x, hp, fx⟩
    isplitl [hp]
    · iexact hp
    · iexists x
      iexact fx

But with current iris-lean iintro fails with icases: cannot destruct iprop(∃ x, Φ x).

How to fix this proof?

By the way, iapply pqr with p, q does not work anymore either, so I had to use

iapply pqr
isplitl [p]
· iexact p
· iexact q

which is a bit more annoying.
I think the syntax for term application has changed, and now it uses $$ instead of with
Have you tried iapply pqr $$ [p] [q]? Or something along those lines
This fails with ispecialize: R is not a wand.
By the way, here's the PR: https://github.com/suhr/iris-tutorial/pull/1. I plan to port other parts of iris-tutorial, but I need to fix the proof of sep_ex_distr first.

Now I'm porting HeapLang specifications, and have the following problem. I have this code and spec:

def arith : Exp := hl(#1 + #2 * #3 + #4 + #5)

theorem arith_spec : ⊢@{IProp GF} WP arith {{ v, ⌜v = hl_val(#16)⌝}} := by
  unfold arith
  istart
  wp_pures
  sorry

As I understand, wp_pures should evaluate pure expressions inside a heaplang expression. But for some reason in this expression it does not evaluate anything.

@suhr I ran into this too. I think more instances of Language.PureExec need to be added/generalized. Right now it looks like the only pure binary op we support is ≤. (see https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/blob/b7161660991216899f212eb33a9da47418655404/Iris/Iris/HeapLang/Instances.lean#L173).

Yeah, it does seem like we could de-duplicate a lot of that file, either with a side lemma or maybe a bit of metaprogramming.
We should definitely fill in the rest of that file!
Personally I don't think I'd bother with metaprogramming it because it just needs to be done once, and the examples sadly aren't all just copy/paste. But if there's something slick then sure

Tactics are not a problem, you can just apply the primitive rules. For example:

theorem cmpXchg_0_to_10_spec (l : Loc) (v : Val) :
  l ↦ v -∗
  WP (cmpXchg_0_to_10 l) {{ _u, (⌜v = hl_val(#0)⌝ ∗ l ↦ hl_val(#10)) ∨
                                (⌜v ≠ hl_val(#0)⌝ ∗ l ↦ v) }} := by
  unfold cmpXchg_0_to_10
  have aa : ProgramLogic.toVal hl(#0) = some hl_val(#0) := rfl
  have bb : ProgramLogic.toVal hl(#10) = some hl_val(#10) := rfl
  if hv: v = hl_val(#0) then
    rw [hv]
    have cc : hl_val(#0).compareSafe hl_val(#0) := rfl
    iintro hl
    iapply wp_cmpXchg_true' _ aa bb cc rfl $$ hl
    intro v''
    iintro ⟨ha, hb⟩
    ileft
    iframe
    ipureintro
    rfl
  else
    iintro hl
    have cc : v.compareSafe hl_val(#0) := by
      have : hl_val(#0).isUnboxed := rfl
      simp [Val.compareSafe, this]
    iapply wp_cmpXchg_fail' _ aa bb cc (decide_eq_false hv) $$ hl
    intro v''
    iintro ⟨ha, hb⟩
    iright
    iframe
    ipureintro
    exact hv

Here I used different versions of wp_cmpXchg_true and wp_cmpXchg_fail, which are more friendly to iapply.

I have found a problem with binding while porting iris-tutorial. Look at the following example which uses par operation:

def par_client : Exp := hl%
  let l1 := ref(#0);
  let l2 := ref(#0);
  ((l1 ← #21) ‖ (l2 ← #2));
  let life := !l1 * !l2;
  (l1, l2, life)

When you later do wp_alloc and wp_bind on this code, l1 is replaced with a location outside the par expression, but not inside the par expression. But l1 clearly should denote the same location everywhere.
In addition, I have noticed that Texan triples are not persistent in Iris-Lean. Why?

suhr said:

In addition, I have noticed that Texan triples are not persistent in Iris-Lean. Why?

This might have just been an oversight on my part. Not a lot of people are using Texan triples yet, so it's easy for it to have been missed. Feel free to open a fix PR, or I can do it later if you will

This seems to be a bug with the ‖ notation which currently wraps both branches in value lambdas, and substitution does not descend into values. Consequently, this goes through on current master:

example (v : Val) :
    Exp.substStr "l1" v hl((l1 ← #21) ‖ (l2 ← #2))
      = hl((l1 ← #21) ‖ (l2 ← #2)) := rfl

Zongyuan Liu said:

It might be a proof mode limitation. In this case rw seems to return no subgoals.

Shall we try ieval (rewrite [← Qp.half_add_half 1]) in Hl instead?

It changes the proof state from:

∗Hl : l ↦ some v
⊢ l ↦{DFrac.own (Qp.half 1)} some v ∗ l ↦{DFrac.own (Qp.half 1)} some v

To:

∗Hl : l ↦{DFrac.own (Qp.half 1 + Qp.half 1)} some v
⊢ l ↦{DFrac.own (Qp.half 1)} some v ∗ l ↦{DFrac.own (Qp.half 1)} some v
The rw tactic closes the subgoal using rfl if possible while rewrite does not.

I have noticed that wp_rec removes ▷ from introduced hypotheses but not from intermediate results constructed with ihave. Should not it remove both? I don't see how inc_spec in linked_list.v could be proved without removing a later from the applied inductive hypothesis.

suhr said:

A rather non-minimal example: https://gist.github.com/suhr/aaeb5a5bf855a39661e4e66a940df44e

It is not an issue of the tactic. It is because the later only guards the premise of the wand.
A proof for the cons case

    | cons x xs ih =>
    iintro %Φ Hil HΦ
    isimp [Functor.map, List.map_cons, isList] in Hil HΦ
    icases Hil with ⟨%hd, %l', %hl, hhd, hxs⟩
    wp_rec
    isimp [hl]
    wp_load
    wp_load
    wp_store
    wp_pures
    iapply ih l' $$ %Φ hxs
    iintro !>Hl
    iapply HΦ
    iexists _, _
    iframe ∗ %hl

In ordinary proofs you can click on a type in Lean Infoview to see the type expression. But in IPM everything is bundled into one IPM goal, and you need multiple clicks to view a particular part of a type.

I almost completed my port of linked_lists.v with only two goals left.

The first goal is

xs : List Int
⊢
⊢ [∗list] x ∈ xs, iprop(∃ i, ⌜x = i⌝)

And the second one is

He1 : (fun x => hl_val(#x)) <$> xs = (fun x => hl_val(#x)) <$> ys
⊢ xs = ys

Both are quite trivial, but I don't see a quick way to close them.
The first one should be provable using bigSepL_intro. For the second one, I am not sure how to best deal with <$> in Lean.
Thanks, that works. Now chapters up to linked_list.v are fully ported.

By the way, now I'm porting invariants.v and I have a yet another observation. Consider the following code:

theorem inv_open_example_attempt_2 (N : Namespace) (l : Loc) :
    inv N (l ↦ hl_val(#1)) ⊢ WP hl(!#l + !#l) {{ v, ⌜v = hl_val(#2)⌝ }} := by
  iintro #Hinv
  -- We now first bind the expression ([!#l]), which _is_ atomic.
  wp_bind !#l
  iinv Hinv with Hl
  · show (nclose N) ⊆ ⊤ ∧ ProgramLogic.Language.Atomic ↑Stuckness.NotStuck hl(!#l)
    simp
    exact instAtomicLoad
  · sorry

The first goal is trivial, and it seems like in Rocq Iris it is closed automatically by the iinv tactic. But in Iris-Lean you need to write this proof manually.

suhr said:

The first goal is trivial, and it seems like in Rocq Iris it is closed automatically by the iinv tactic. But in Iris-Lean you need to write this proof manually.

iinv uses iSolveSidecondition to attempt closing the goal. The corresponding Ltac for solving side conditions in Rocq uses split_and?; try solve [ fast_done | solve_ndisj | tc_solve ].

With the fix in the latest PR, it should be solved automatically.

I have found a yet another pain point while porting iris-tutorial. Consider the following code (ported from gr_predicates.v):

def is_list_pre (Φ : Val → IProp GF) (f : Val → IProp GF) (v : Val) : IProp GF := iprop%
  ⌜v = hl_val(none())⌝ ∨
    ∃ l : Loc, ⌜v = hl_val(some(#l))⌝ ∗ ∃ x t, l ↦ hl_val((&x, &t)) ∗ Φ x ∗ f t

instance is_list_pre_mono (Φ : Val → IProp GF) :
    @BIMonoPred _ _ _ (OFE.ofDiscrete Val) (is_list_pre Φ) := by
  refine @BIMonoPred.mk _ _ _ (OFE.ofDiscrete Val) _ ?_ ?_
  · iintro %Ψ1 %Ψ2 %_ %_ #H1 %x H2
    unfold is_list_pre
    icases H2 with (H | ⟨%l, Hx, ⟨%x', %t, Hl, HΦx, H⟩⟩)
    · ileft; iframe
    · iright
      iexists l
      iframe
      iapply H1 $$ H
  · unfold is_list_pre
    sorry

Not only specifying OFE.ofDiscrete Val everywhere is quite annoying, but also in the second branch infer_instance cannot infer the instance.
...but it looks like this instance in iris-tutorial is actually useless. Strange.
What is the OFE structure on Val?

Have you tried 

instance : OFE Val := OFE.ofDiscrete _
Indeed, I totally forgot I can just do local instance.

Rocq Iris has a small feature that Iris-Lean still lacks: destructing with rewrites. For example:

  (**
    Open the invariant, strip the later from the equality (achieved by
    [">"]), and rewrite with the equality (achieved by ["->"]).
  *)
  iInv "Hinv" as "[>-> HP]".

Do we need this feature in Iris-Lean?

suhr said:

Rocq Iris has a small feature that Iris-Lean still lacks: destructing with rewrites. For example:

  (**
    Open the invariant, strip the later from the equality (achieved by
    [">"]), and rewrite with the equality (achieved by ["->"]).
  *)
  iInv "Hinv" as "[>-> HP]".

Do we need this feature in Iris-Lean?

Does >%rfl provide the expected feature?

Example:

example [BI PROP] [BIUpdate PROP] (P : PROP) : (|==> P) ∗ (|==> <affine> ⌜x = 0⌝) ⊢ |==> (P ∗ ⌜x = 0⌝) := by
  iintro H
  icases H with ⟨>HP, >%rfl⟩
  isplitl [HP]
  · iexact HP
  · imodintro
    ipureintro
    rfl
or more generally %rfl for rewrites using equalities, where rfl is the rcases pattern for rewriting
Yes, it works! But https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/blob/master/Iris/tactics.md does not say a word about it.
It is implicitly part of rcasesPat (rcases pattern). Perhaps we can make it clearer in the documentation.
